newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch retailer Unigro slams competition bill.
newsitem.headline: Dutch retailer Unigro slams competition bill.

text.p: Chairman Rob ter Haar of Dutch grocery store chain Unigro on Monday lashed out at a bill aimed at enhancing retail sector competition, saying it would hike Dutch food prices.
The bill aims to increase free competition in the Dutch food retail sector by prohibiting independent retailers from entering into exclusive purchasing agreements with suppliers.

But Ter Haar, whose company is set to merge with sector rival De Boer Winkelbedrijven to create the country's second largest supermarket chain, said the law would stop chains investing in franchise formulas with independent operators.

"As a result of the limitations (economic affairs minister Hans) Wijers plans to introduce, it will no longer be attractive for store chains to invest in independent outlet- and franchising structures," he said.

This would lead to reduced rather than enhanced competition, he said. Independent operators could then no longer join large-scale purchasing combines which enabled them to benefit from economies of scale.
"The bill will not be advantageous to the Dutch food sector. Food in the Netherlands is the cheapest in Europe, exclusive purchasing agreements keep us on our toes," he said.
Ter Haar would not give a figure of the possible impact introduction of the bill in its present form would have on his own company.

Unlisted Unigro and merger partner De Boer Winkelbedrijven work extensively with franchising agreements and together are members of purchasing combine Superunie, which represents consumer turnover of some 13 billion guilders.
